windows CI leg no longer fails intermittently with \\u0027The process cannot access the file\\u0027 on a node home\\u0027s daemon.json or coanda.db, because the CLI reads the daemon\\u0027s address file safely while the daemon writes it, and nothing in the test process still holds coanda.db once the export and the rebuild have returned.\u0022},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022No coa command fails with an IOException because it read daemon.json while the daemon was writing it: a reader that meets the file mid-write treats the daemon as not yet answering and looks again, as it does today for a file it cannot parse. A test holds daemon.json open the way DaemonInfo.Save does and shows that DaemonInfo.Load, and the CLI\\u0027s search for a running daemon, return without throwing; the pull request says whether that test fails on the windows leg without the fix.\u0022,\u0022The pull request names what held coanda.db when RecordExportTests.A_rebuild_that_fails_part_way_leaves_the_home_as_it_found_it failed hashing the home\\u0027s files (RecordExportTests.cs:425, through RecordHomes.Files), gives the evidence that established it, and fixes that holder where it is opened. If it is a connection this code or the store library opened, the export and the rebuild release it before they return, so a rebuild\\u0027s move of coanda.db cannot meet it either.\u0022,\u0022After the fix, RecordExportTests and DaemonStartTests pass in at least 20 consecutive repeated runs of those two classes on Windows, on the windows CI runner or a Windows machine, and the pull request gives the command, where it ran, and the result. Any workflow change made only to repeat them is gone from the branch before it merges.\u0022,\u0022No test is skipped, retried, wrapped in a retry loop, given a longer wait, or changed to read the home\\u0027s files with a wider share mode, and no test\\u0027s assertions change. If what held coanda.db turns out to be outside the test process, the session records that evidence in its journal and stops rather than loosening a test.\u0022,\u0022dotnet build --configuration Release succeeds with warnings as errors, and dotnet test --configuration Release --no-build passes on both CI legs.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022## Why\\n\\nThe windows-latest CI leg fails intermittently with System.IO.IOException \\u0027The process cannot access the file\\u0027, and each failure costs a fix lap on whatever pull request meets it. Phase 3\\u0027s gate also runs the real rebuild on the Windows machine. The failures seen so far have two different causes, and neither matches the first guess that a pooled SQLite connection blocked a move.\\n\\n1. **daemon.json, a read during a write.** On PR #73, DaemonStartTests.Daemon_start_with_its_output_piped_returns_and_leaves_the_daemon_running failed because \\u0060coa daemon start\\u0060 printed an IOException on \\u0060daemon.json\\u0060, not on coanda.db. The stack runs DaemonClient.EnsureRunningAsync, then FindRunningAsync (src/Coanda.Cli/DaemonClient.cs:79), then DaemonInfo.Load (src/Coanda.Daemon/Api/DaemonInfo.cs:31). Save (DaemonInfo.cs:18) holds the file open for writing with FileShare.Read, and Load\\u0027s File.ReadAllText asks for FileShare.Read too, which Windows refuses while a write handle is open. Load catches only JsonException. The start command polls every 200 ms while the daemon writes the file, so the window is real on every start. This is a product defect, not only a test one. Note that writing to a temporary file and renaming it over daemon.json moves the failure to the daemon\\u0027s side on Windows, since a reader opened without FileShare.Delete blocks the rename.\\n2. **coanda.db, held after the export.** On main at fb402ea (after PR #71), RecordExportTests.A_rebuild_that_fails_part_way_leaves_the_home_as_it_found_it failed at RecordExportTests.cs:425, where RecordHomes.Files (tests/Coanda.Tests/Daemon/RecordHomes.cs:217) hashes coanda.db with File.ReadAllBytes. No daemon runs in that test. Before that line, RecordHomes.WriteAsync (the extended home) and RecordExport.WriteAsync have both returned. Every direct connection on that path already opens with pooling off (RecordExport.Connect and ConnectUnchanged, RecordHomes.Open, EarlierProjectRecords), and each store opened through StoreConfiguration.Open is disposed and followed by SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools (RecordExport.cs:77, RecordHomes.cs:115). So something else held the file: a connection the store library opened that was not disposed or was opened after the pools were cleared, or a handle outside the process. Find out which before fixing.\\n\\nThe two Neither_runs_while_a_daemon tests that failed during PR #69 were fixed inside that pull request: AssertRefusedAsync now leaves the running daemon\\u0027s files out of the comparison (OutsideTheDaemon, RecordExportTests.cs:450). They stay in the repeated runs as a regression check and need no change.\\n\\n## Where to look\\n\\n- src/Coanda.Daemon/Api/DaemonInfo.cs and its two readers: src/Coanda.Cli/DaemonClient.cs (FindRunningAsync, EnsureRunningAsync) and src/Coanda.Daemon/Api/Endpoints/DaemonEndpoints.cs:20.\\n- src/Coanda.Daemon/Store/RecordExport.cs (ExportAsync), RecordRebuild.cs (BuildAsync, Compare, Swap), StoreConfiguration.cs (Open, Configure), and tests/Coanda.Tests/Daemon/RecordHomes.cs (ExtendAsync, PublishGatedBuildAsync, Files).\\n- .github/workflows/ci.yml has no manual trigger, so repeating a test class on the windows runner means a temporary step on the pull request\\u0027s branch.\\n\\n## Ruling (orchestrator, 2026-11-05, on Brian\\u0027s behalf)\\n\\nThe daemon.json sharing defect (DaemonInfo.cs:18 and :31, reproducing on every Windows open while a write handle is held) ships in this pull request whatever the coanda.db diagnosis finds. If the coanda.db violation does not reproduce in the recorded attempts, the pull request still merges with the daemon.json fix, any connection-release change justified by reading the code, and a record of the attempts, rather than stopping with nothing.\\n\\n## Non-goals\\n\\nNo change to the store\\u0027s schema, to what the export writes or the rebuild builds, to daemon.json\\u0027s content or location, or to any test\\u0027s assertions. No new CI leg and no permanent change to the CI workflow. The SQLite \\u0027unable to open database file\\u0027 errors the trigger loop and the module feed log in other tests\\u0027 output are not part of this task.\u0022},\u0022BlockedBy\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Type\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022},\u0022Model\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022RevisedAt\u0022:\u00222026-11-05T23:10:36.338638\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022RevisedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022EpicId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022QueuePriority\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageComposition\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageCompositionAcknowledged\u0022:false,\u0022ClearInteractiveMode\u0022:false,\u0022StackedOnTaskId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022StackedOnPullRequestNumber\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022CloseLinkedIssue\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022SpikeKind\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ExitCriterion\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Constraints\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Effort\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022HumanGate\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022RefinementSessionId\u0022:null}","originEventId":"afa5faf8-b74e-478f-a4ca-97d46aa86111","originSequence":171998,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-11-05T23:10:36.34798+00:00","originProjectId":"01a1a29e-778a-7730-9f07-304d9ac0ffeb"}]
